In a cumulative-logit proportional-odds ordinal regression of COVID-19 severity on all 1,000 subjects — outcome = subject-level maximum health-status score (0–7) over documented COVID-19 AE rows (0 = no COVID-19 AE; WHO clinical-progression scale), predictors = BCG (TRTGRP=='BCG'), any prior medical history (567/1000), the BCG×history interaction, and patients_seen (ordinal 1–3) as the interaction-frequency control — the interaction odds ratio is OR = 1.298 (95% CI 0.663–2.540, Wald p = 0.446).

In words: the effect of prior medical history on COVID-19 severity is an estimated ≈30% larger (×1.30) in BCG-vaccinated participants than in placebo, but this is not statistically significant and the CI spans from a ~34% protective interaction to a ~2.5-fold exacerbating interaction. Main effects: BCG OR = 0.96 (p = 0.88), prior-history OR = 1.58 (p = 0.058), patients_seen OR = 1.64 (p = 0.001; the control is strong and significant).

Sensitivity (so the estimate moves with): the interaction is essentially insensitive to the frequency-control choice (1.298 with patients_seen vs 1.34–1.36 with expect_interact/work_hours, 1.33 without a control) and to history-as-count (1.08 per condition). It is most sensitive to SEVERITY CODING: restricting to the 189 subjects with a documented COVID-19 AE reverses the point estimate (HS 1–7: OR 0.75, p = 0.64; AESEV 1–4: OR 0.73, p = 0.66), while widening severity to all RTI events attenuates it (OR 1.09, p = 0.72). Every construction has CIs spanning 1. Proportional-odds is formally rejected (Brant-type LR χ² = 382, df = 4, p < 0.0001 — driven by the heavily zero-inflated severity, 812/1000 zeros), but the non-PO threshold sensitivities keep the interaction small and non-significant (any-COVID threshold OR = 1.32, p = 0.41; moderate+ threshold OR = 0.99, p = 0.98; severe+ threshold unstable, n = 22), so the conclusion holds under partial/non-PO.

Conclusion: there is no statistically significant interaction between BCG vaccination and prior medical history on COVID-19 severity; the primary interaction OR is 1.30 (95% CI 0.66–2.54, p = 0.45), and the estimate is dominated by the severity-coding choice (full-population 0–7 vs infected-only 1–7/AESEV), not by history definition or the adjustment control.
